concept: The closed select is a field, a groove like Input. The open list is an opaque sheet whose rows nest its corner, so each row radius is the sheet radius minus an inset that is the same on every side. The highlighted row is a lens with light on its top edge, and the check leads the chosen row.

root.why: label above the control, the order people read a form in

label.why: a visible label that is also the accessible name of the control

hidden.why: when the context names the control, the label stays for screen readers and is hidden visually

trigger.why: the closed control is the same groove as Input, a dimmed recess with a lit bottom lip, so a form reads as one family

sm.why: small is 32px for toolbars and top bars

md.why: medium is the 44px touch size for forms

icon.why: the chevron says this opens a list, a cue that does not rely on hover

chevron.why: the chevron turns over when the list is open, showing the state by shape

menu.why: an opaque sheet (D-017) with the same inset on all four sides, so every row sits evenly inside its corner

viewport.why: rows stack with a hairline gap inside the even inset, so the inset reads larger than the gap and the list reads as one

item.why: a row nests the sheet corner, its radius computed as the sheet radius minus the inset, and rows are tall enough that the corner never becomes a pill

check.why: a check marks the chosen option, so the choice is shown by a mark and not by colour alone

slot.why: a fixed space at the start of every row for the check, so the chosen row is marked first and labels stay aligned

hover.why: hover adds a hairline ring over the groove, answering the pointer without moving anything

disabled.why: disabled cannot open, uses the shared disabled opacity, and keeps its label readable

focus-visible.why: keyboard focus draws the shared ring with its halo so the focused control is visible on any scene

data-placeholder.why: an empty control shows its placeholder in the measured secondary colour

data-state=open.why: while open, the chevron turns to show the list belongs to this control

data-highlighted.why: the highlighted row is a lens lit on its top edge, with a glint under the pointer when a pointer is there

data-state=checked.why: the chosen option is semibold as well as checked

data-disabled.why: unavailable options stay visible at half opacity so the reader knows they exist

@media forced-colors: active.why: forced colours draw real borders and a highlight outline so the list and the current row stay visible

data-pane-card=glass.why: the trigger drops the card text halo because its groove already gives the label its ground

box-shadow.why: the ring change eases at hover pace so the pointer response reads as one calm event

transform.why: the chevron turns over the hover duration so the state change is followed by the eye

@menu-in.why: the list drops a few pixels from the control and settles, so it reads as coming from it

default_to_avoid.pattern: the Radix or Material dropdown: a padded card with pill-shaped rows whose corner does not follow the card's, a check at the far end
default_to_avoid.why_not: the highlighted row's corner bulged against the flyout's (24px corner, 4px inset, 18px rows on 32px), so the two curves fought; the closed trigger measured 2.65:1 in light (R-008)

derivation.consequence: corners are continuous and nest, so an inner surface's radius is the outer radius minus the padding between them and a pane inside a pane reads as inside it
derivation.form: a row's radius is computed as the sheet radius minus the inset, and the inset is the same on all four sides

derivation.consequence: a soft shadow below and a rim of light on the top-left edge say where the pane floats
derivation.form: the highlighted row is a lens with light on its top edge, never a flat grey block

derivation.consequence: nothing moves on its own; every motion answers something the reader did
derivation.form: the lens carries a glint under the pointer; keyboard highlight shows the lens without the glint

derivation.consequence: selected and pressed states change shape or add a mark (a check, a ring), never only colour
derivation.form: the chosen row has a check at its start, read first, and a heavier weight

derivation.consequence: legibility comes from dimming and blurring the backdrop (brightness, blur), never from an opaque tint
derivation.form: the closed trigger is the same groove as Input, so a form reads as one family

variants.reason: A and B both fix the nesting P3 asks for; B also makes the highlight a lit lens (P3 depth) and leads with the check (P6), as visionOS menus do. C avoids nesting by clipping and adds dividers that a menu of four rows does not need, and its first and last highlight meet the corner unevenly.
